recent_developments: ~6 months ago the company signed a LANDMARK multi-generation compute partnership with a leading AI-model developer: 6 gigawatts of its accelerators to be deployed over several years, the first gigawatt starting the SECOND HALF of this year on its next-gen rack-scale platform. The counterparty received a warrant for up to ~10% of the company, vesting on deployment milestones AND share-price targets. The stock re-rated ~+24% on announcement day.

Execution since the deal: two record quarterly prints in a row (+36% and +34% revenue YoY), Data Center accelerating (+39% last quarter), gross margin expanding, and essentially NONE of the partnership revenue is in numbers or guidance yet.
Export walls partially lifted: licenses were granted for limited China-market accelerator sales (a token ~135 in the current-quarter guide, vs zero for most of last year).

BEAR — concentration and circularity: the 6GW partner is the industry's most aggressively levered capex bettor and is simultaneously a customer, a warrant-holder and a rival buyer of a competing platform; the warrant structure has vendor-financing optics, and full vesting means up to ~10% dilution. If AI capex pauses, the deal's out-year gigawatts may never convert.

BEAR — competitive response: the category leader still commands ~90% of the accelerator market with the default software ecosystem and its own next-generation cycle shipping this year; hyperscalers continue scaling in-house custom silicon. The company must execute a rack-scale platform transition — a discipline it has never delivered at this scale — on schedule for the partnership's first tranche.

BEAR — valuation: ~77x trailing GAAP earnings and ~9.5x trailing sales pre-pays for years of deployment; the stock has gone sideways-to-down for four months and is -23% off its high as the market debates whether the AI-infrastructure buildout is sustainable or a circular-financing bubble.
